title: Zugzwang of Zugzwangs
reviewNotes: Full five-piece physical diagram visually reconstructed. Four branches: Qc2+ Kd8 Qc7+ Ke8 Ka4 Qf7 Qc8 mate; both premature queen and knight checks draw; independent Kb8 alternative mates. Ka4 denies Qa3 and retains the Qe7 threat. All seven contact sheets reviewed, clear root and final board enlarged.
transcript: White's brilliant idea's queen to c2, check, forcing the black king between a rock and a hard place. There are four possible moves for this black king, but actually most of them will simply lead to a checkmate in just a matter of a few moves. For example, like this. But what is actually interesting is what happens when the king decides to go to this side of the board. Now, of course, we are going to give a check with the white queen, getting closer to that black king and pushing him further to the right. And now it might seem like there is no way to make any progress. If we give a check with the queen, for example, down here, the king is actually going to be able to escape. And now this is likely to fizzle out to a draw. And giving a check with the knight, well, would simply lose the knight. And again, [music] this is just a draw. But believe it or not, white has an incredible idea and a beautiful move that will allow him to win this position. And that move, the only move that wins, is the majestic king to a4. Stepping away from the action, and yet this move is taking away a critical escape square for the black queen. And what is in front of us now is a zugzwang, a situation where black would like to not have to move any piece to be able to draw the position. You see, black has to remain defending this square because if the queen moves away, well, this is just going to be a checkmate in one move. But incredibly, despite this being a queen and having the fully open board that it can go to, there's nowhere that the queen can go while also keeping track of this square. Both of these are defended by the white queen. Every single square on this diagonal is either covered by the king or by the queen [music] or by the knight. This square is covered by the knight, and the queen cannot even give a check to the white king because of another defense by the knight. So, the only square from where the black queen can defend this square while also not being captured is f7. From here, the king defends the queen and the queen defends checkmate. But unfortunately, the queen is also now taking away the only escape square of the king, meaning that queen to C8 will be now a checkmate. If you like this board, read the caption.
